raw_case_text:
A 22-year-old male was evaluated at the ED on March 24, 2014, because of a 3-day history of fever, malaise, myalgia, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache. Physical examination revealed fever, underweight (body mass index = 18.1), and tachycardia. He was given acetaminophen and discharged from the ED with a diagnosis of viral syndrome.
Serum collected on day 2 of illness was negative by PCR and MAT. Convalescent serum collected 18 days after illness onset was positive by MAT with a reciprocal titer of 800 against serogroups Bataviae (serovar Bataviae) and Canicola (serovar Canicola) and was also positive for detection of anti-dengue virus IgM antibodies.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-year-old male presenting with a 3-day history of fever, malaise, myalgia, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented to the emergency department on March 24, 2014, with a 3-day history of fever, malaise, myalgias, nausea, rhinorrhea, sore throat, and headache. Following clinical examination, he received symptomatic therapy and was discharged home with a diagnosis of viral syndrome.

objective.physical_examination: Physical examination revealed fever, tachycardia, and an underweight body habitus with a body mass index (BMI) of 18.1 kg/m2.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Leptospirosis with dengue virus co-infection. Convalescent serum obtained 18 days post-onset demonstrated positive MAT with a reciprocal titer of 800 against serogroups Bataviae (serovar Bataviae) and Canicola (serovar Canicola), alongside positive anti-dengue virus IgM antibodies. Acute-phase serum drawn on illness day 2 was negative by both PCR and MAT.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with oral acetaminophen in the emergency department for presumptive viral syndrome and discharged home with uneventful recovery.
